study_name.evidence_quote: Integrated multi-omics of the human gut microbiome in a case study of familial type 1 diabetes
study_name.notes: Study name inferred from first author and publication year

target_condition.evidence_quote: samples from four families with multiple cases of type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM)

body_site.evidence_quote: analysis of intra- and inter-individual variation demonstrates that family membership has a pronounced effect on the structural and functional composition of the gastrointestinal microbiome
body_site.notes: Explicitly stated as faecal samples throughout

sequencing_platform.evidence_quote: DNA was sequenced with 101 bp per paired end on a HiSeq2000 system (Illumina)
sequencing_platform.section: Methods — Metagenomic DNA and RNA sequencing

country.evidence_quote: from existing patient cohorts from the Centre Hospitalier du Luxembourg
country.section: Methods — Anthropometric, nutritional, clinical data and blood and stool sampling
country.notes: All participants from Luxembourg Centre for Systems Biomedicine and affiliated institutions

dna_extraction_kit.notes: PowerSoil Kit used for DNA extraction

lifestyle.notes: No lifestyle category (hunter-gatherer, agriculturalist, etc.) reported

disease.section: Abstract; Study cohort and microbial community structures
disease.notes: Study included both individuals with T1DM and healthy family members as control group.

value: Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM) - diagnosed >5 years, controlled by insulin

by_subgroup.Individuals with T1DM: Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM) - diagnosed >5 years, controlled by insulin

biomarker_name.evidence_quote: AMY2A and AMY2B, carboxypeptidase CPA1 and the less characterised CUZD1, to be less abundant in the stool of individuals with T1DM
biomarker_name.section: Results — Human protein excretion in T1DM and microbial functions
biomarker_name.notes: Multiple biomarkers identified across different omic levels; some are human proteins (AMY2A, AMY2B, etc.) and others are microbial functions (thiazole synthase, catalase, etc.)

biomarker_unit.evidence_quote: Relative protein abundances of human AMY2A (a) and AMY2B (b). Boxes span the first to third quartiles, the central thick bars represent the medians
biomarker_unit.notes: Units vary by biomarker type; human proteins reported as relative abundance, microbial genes as transcript/transcript abundance

biomarker_value.notes: Paper reports qualitative differences and correlations but does not provide absolute numeric values for biomarker measurements in a summary table

disease_response_os.notes: This is a microbiome composition study, not an oncology or mortality study; OS not applicable

disease_response_os_unit.notes: Not applicable to this study design

ecog_performance_status.notes: ECOG performance status not measured or reported in this microbiome study

feces_phenotype_value.evidence_quote: Analysis of intra- and inter-individual variation demonstrates that family membership has a pronounced effect on the structural and functional composition of the gastrointestinal microbiota.
feces_phenotype_value.notes: Fecal phenotypes characterized through multi-omic analysis (metagenomic, metatranscriptomic, metaproteomic); family-dependent clustering and T1DM-associated differences in functional profiles observed

tumor_size_measurement.notes: Not an oncology study; tumor size not relevant

tumor_size_residual_measurement.notes: Not applicable to this microbiome study

value: Study cohort: 20 individuals from 4 families with at least 2 generations presenting 2+ cases of T1DM
53 well-preserved faecal samples collected over 2-4 months
T1DM diagnosed >5 years, controlled by insulin
Metaproteomic data: 185,000 ± 13,000 peptide mass spectra per sample
De novo assembly: 287 ± 43 Mbp total contig length
2,400 ± 1,600 microbial and 200 ± 70 human protein groups identified per sample
43 ± 14% of microorganisms belonged to mOTUs without sequenced isolate genome
Family membership stratifies microbiome more than age or BMI
No consistent taxonomic differences across families in T1DM
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: The study cohort consisted of 20 individuals from four families of at least two generations presenting at least two cases of T1DM. Analysis... of 53 well-preserved faecal samples collected over a period of two to four months.
uncurated_metadata.notes: Comprehensive multi-omic study design with extensive technical details; integration of metagenomic, metatranscriptomic, and metaproteomic data

host_species.evidence_quote: The study cohort consisted of 20 individuals from four families of at least two generations presenting at least two cases of T1DM
host_species.section: Methods — Study cohort and microbial community structures
host_species.notes: Human participants explicitly described as individuals with familial type 1 diabetes mellitus; whole-genome sequencing performed on human participants

extraction_warnings: Subject-level demographic data (age, sex, ancestry) not provided in main text; referenced in Supplementary Table 1 which is not included.
Case/control status not explicitly assigned per sample; families included both T1DM-affected and unaffected members but individual designations not listed.
Exact collection dates and days_from_first_collection not provided; study was longitudinal with visits 2-4 weeks apart.
Sample IDs derived from figure labels (M##.#-V#); no formal sample accession numbers provided except BioProject PRJNA289586.
Only 18 of 20 individuals had complete multi-omic analysis; 2 individuals (M01.5, M03.1) metagenomic-only per Figure 1b caption.
Metatranscriptomic sequencing used IlluminaHiSeq2500 (150 bp paired-end), not HiSeq2000; platform field standardized to 'IlluminaHiSeq'.
Batch 1 returned granularity='subgroup_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.
Batch 1 subgroups ['Individuals with T1DM', 'Healthy relatives'] differ from batch 0 []; kept batch 0.

Paper contains extensive clinical and demographic data referenced in supplementary tables (Supplementary Table 1 and others) that are not provided in the full text. Many fields marked 'not_reported' because the supplementary data are inaccessible.
Study design is observational case study of families, not a clinical trial or treatment response study, so many oncology-related fields are not applicable.
Granularity set to 'subgroup_level' to distinguish between individuals with T1DM and healthy relatives, which is the primary stratification in the paper.
Batch 2 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.
Biomarker values not provided as absolute numbers; only relative abundances and correlations reported
Multiple biomarker types across different omic levels (proteins, transcripts, genes) with heterogeneous units
Study is case study of small cohort (n=20 from 4 families); results not generalizable
Disease response measures (OS, ECOG, tumor size) not applicable to this microbiome study design
Fecal phenotypes characterized indirectly through multi-omic composition analysis rather than direct phenotypic measurements
